A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same INTP preference-alignment research. All 20 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original TTS alignment experiments, human evaluations, data ablations and iterative Ints alignment results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds an Ints evaluation on four languages not covered by INTP in Appendix E.2.

M1.justification: INTP construction, the AR, flow-matching and masked-model DPO procedures, Ints architecture and iterative alignment remain unchanged. The added language evaluation tests the existing method.

E1.justification: Appendix E.2 adds Japanese, Korean, German and French speech evaluation using GTSinger, substantially broadening evaluation beyond v1's English/Chinese scenarios. These languages are absent from INTP, and GTSinger is reported as unused in pre-training and post-training.

E2.justification: The retained experiments use the same models and controls, including ARS, F5-TTS, MaskGCT, CosyVoice 2, Ints and the SFT control. The new GTSinger experiment extends the existing Ints versus Ints-with-INTP comparison without introducing another comparator.

E3.justification: The new experiment specifies 500 evaluation samples per added language and compares Ints before and after alignment using WER and SIM. Existing training settings, evaluation sample counts, metrics and listening-test procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E.2 adds a focused generalization analysis testing whether English/Chinese preference alignment transfers to other languages on an unused dataset. Existing data-type, model-source, negative-sample and language ablations are retained, including v1 Appendix G as v2 Appendix E.1.

E5.justification: The N-CMOS uncertainty reporting in Table 4 and repeated human assessments in Appendix F.3 are unchanged. The new language results are point estimates and introduce no additional run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing experimental values are retained, including v1 Table 10 as v2 Table 9. New Table 10 reports lower WER and higher SIM after Ints alignment in all four added languages; for example, Korean WER is 31.67 without alignment versus 19.57 with INTP, and SIM is 0.708 versus 0.741.

T1.justification: Equations 1–17 and the AR, flow-matching and masked-model derivations are unchanged. The derivation appendix moves from C to B without substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions: INTP, DPO extensions across architectures, weak-to-strong transfer and iterative alignment. The added language evidence does not redefine these main claims.

C2.justification: v2 extends the existing foundational-intelligibility interpretation to languages outside INTP, hypothesizing that improved basic articulation and pronunciation explain the new transfer results. Earlier interpretations and the stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v1 promises future release through a general Amphion link; v2 reports open-sourcing and adds specific access links for INTP, aligned models and evaluation data. This materially expands resource-access information. Implementation settings remain unchanged, and Appendix A.1 still describes some generation scripts as future releases.

R1.justification: v2 adds the GTSinger citation for its new evaluation. The related-work discussion retains its substance. DualCodec's anonymous citation is replaced by its named publication, while FunASR and Paraformer receive bibliographic updates; these are existing works, not new research positioning.

P1.justification: Related work moves from Appendix A to Section 2, and supplementary results are grouped under Appendix E. v2 also adds an acknowledgment and makes limited wording edits. Most prose remains verbatim.

P2.justification: v2 adds the unseen-language results table and relocates existing displays during reflow. v1 Tables 9 and 10 become v2 Tables 11 and 9, respectively. Existing figures and retained tables preserve their content and basic visual design.

improvement.justification: The new four-language evaluation provides useful additional evidence for transfer beyond INTP's languages, and specific resource links improve reproducibility information. The gain is bounded: the new test covers only Ints and does not specify the WER procedure for the added languages, while some script-release wording remains inconsistent. The core methods and existing evidence are otherwise stable.
